why_this_target: ASSOCIATE is unusually good fixture material because the association is genuinely observable: the associate name's type, kind, length, rank and bounds are specified by the standard, definability lets an assignment through the associate name be observed on the selector, and construct-entity scoping is directly testable against an outer homonym.

oracle_justification.why_legitimate: These are used as oracles only because the standard REQUIRES the asserted values, not because they are merely typical, and each plan states that justification. The packet does not claim to be testing those intrinsics themselves.
oracle_justification.character_discipline: Every length assertion uses LEN explicitly and never a character comparison, because comparison blank-pads the shorter operand and could otherwise succeed for the wrong reason.

compiler_observations.caveat: ASSOCIATE with strided array-section selectors is exactly where a compiler may be wrong, so the independently recomputed bounds - not the agreement between compilers - are what validate these fixtures.

explicit_limitations: 10 facets are established; 23 remain pending, most blocked on unregistered Clause 15 or Clause 19 material, polymorphism, coarrays or branch ownership.
The scoping fixture demonstrates outer-homonym preservation for this construct. It does not establish full Clause 19 scope and lifetime coverage.
The bounds fixtures rely on standard LBOUND, UBOUND, SHAPE and SIZE inquiry semantics; they do not test those intrinsics independently.
No kind, polymorphism, coarray, pointer, allocatable, optional, contiguity or branch diagnostic coverage is claimed.

corrective_action.issue: Binding facets into a catalogue changes its content and therefore STALES its content-bound source review by design. Batches 118, 119 and 120 each left such staleness uncorrected and were committed with it.
corrective_action.how_it_surfaced: The full-suite gate for this batch FAILED with 'cannot review linked evidence: 11.1.3.3: catalogue source review is stale', raised from test_derived_value_links case 32. The earlier batches' gates had passed only because no test case happened to exercise the affected catalogues through the linked-evidence path.
corrective_action.remedy: All six catalogue source reviews were renewed. Each renewal records that the staleness is attributable SOLELY to facet binding; that the SOURCE ACCOUNTING IS UNCHANGED, with no base or fine unit added, removed or redispositioned, no requirement added or deleted, and no requirement identifier renumbered or reused; and that the renewal carries the original independent source review forward without adding any new source claim. It is not fixture approval, which is recorded separately per case, and confers no extra execution or coverage credit.
corrective_action.verification: After renewal the only non-reviewed catalogue is 18.3.7, which was already 'draft' at session start commit 839d058 and was never touched by this session. The full suite then ran 984 tests OK.
corrective_action.process_lesson: A FIXTURE packet must renew the source review of every catalogue it binds facets into, as part of the same integration. This is now recorded in the integration checklist.
